Title: edge0 — streaming-MoE inference: SSD expert offload + Recover-LoRA + prerouter
Summary: An Apache-2.0 Python framework that runs sparse-MoE models far larger than available RAM by **mmapping expert weights off SSD** and predicting routing one step ahead so the loads overlap the forward pass. Two ready-to-run 4-bit tiers ship with trained LoRA + prerouter adapters. Verified at capture: **14 stars**, created 2026-09-08 — a two-day-old repo whose numbers are entirely self-reported.

Title: adamzweiger/compaction — official code for "Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching
Summary: Reference implementation for [[2026-02-18-am-fast-kv-compaction-attention-matching]]. MIT license, **263 stars** at capture, Python, last pushed 2026-04-22. Supports Qwen3, Llama, and Gemma3 models; ships a one-line demo (`examples/qa_demo.py`) that compacts a KV cache to 10% and compares QA accuracy before/after.

Title: SoL-Pi (NVIDIA) — recursively scaling auto-research loops to find 4 reusable token-efficiency mechanisms for the Pi coding agent: 44.7–49.0% token reduction, ~1/3 cost cut, comparable task performance
Summary: SoL-Pi (MIT, **2,670★**) is NVIDIA's standalone, opt-in extension for the [Pi coding agent](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), built by running "scaled auto-research loops" that searched for ways to make the harness itself more token-efficient without changing task behavior. Four mechanisms survived that search — **Action Fusion**, **ObservationPack**, an **Evidence-Preserving Reducer**, and **Online Context Compact** — each opt-in, each composed through Pi's public extension API with no source patches. On EdgeBench (51 tasks), the paper (arXiv:2609.20519) reports **44.7–49.0% token-traffic reduction** and roughly a **1/3 cost reduction**, at comparable performance to the baseline harness.

Title: Jev Reproductions Tracker (multimodalart, HF Space) — 36 open rebuilds of TypeSafe's Jev / System One in five kinds, with what is still not in the open
Summary: A static HF Space (13 likes, created 2026-09-17 20:05 UTC, data = one `ITEMS` JS array in `index.html`) that tracks **36 artifacts** rebuilding TypeSafe's **Jev** — the "System One" decision model (state + typed questions with fixed options → one-pass probability distributions, no text generation; trained with "RLCD", Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions) launched ~2026-09-15 — sorted by a trending score (♥ X likes + 5 × GitHub stars + 8 × Hub likes + views ÷ 500). Five kinds: **Decoding** (parallel constrained decoding on stock weights — 14 entries), **Trained** (scoring heads / fine-tunes — 12, one promised), **Diffusion** (2), **Prior art** (2), **Explainers** (6). Its own verdict on what is *not* in the open after 48 hours: TypeSafe's weights, the RLCD algorithm/loss/data, and any open model matching Jev's calibration claims — "the best local study reports ~74% agreement with Jev vs Jev's own 87% on the same subset, and finds confidence does not reliably flag errors."

Title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills (DisCo / AREX-Skill)
Summary: Names the missing layer in autonomous ML-research agents **operational knowledge** — "the know-how that separates knowing a method from making it work" — and argues it should be distilled out of repos and papers into **Agent Skills** ahead of time, not rediscovered per run. **DisCo** is the distiller; the output is the **AREX-Skill Library**: 5,353 skills from 1,000 ML repos, 20 areas, 178 capability families. With backbone (GPT-5.5 via Codex), harness, and run-time budget held fixed, skills lift MLE-bench Any-Medal **31.11% → 72.89%** (+134.3% relative). Full text: [repo-to-skill-disco.txt](../assets/repo-to-skill-disco.txt) · PDF: [repo-to-skill-disco.pdf](../assets/repo-to-skill-disco.pdf) (48pp).

Title: classifier.dev (mrmps) — a free, keyless zero-shot classification API in front of real Jev: measured calibration (82% right at ≥0.9 confidence), a model-fallback chain, and the feedback.now agent-reporting protocol
Summary: [classifier.dev](https://classifier.dev) (MIT, **372★**) is a live, production Cloudflare Worker offering free zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP with no API key — `curl https://classifier.dev/spam,not+spam/Win+a+free+iPhone` → `spam`. It answers primarily from **real TypeSafe Jev** (via Vercel's AI Gateway, which serves Jev on a free monthly credit; falls back to a direct TypeSafe key, then OpenRouter), batching up to 1,000 texts into one upstream call. It's the first source in this vault reporting **measured, independent calibration numbers for Jev in production**: at ≥0.9 confidence, answers were right **82%** of the time on a 400-item six-way emotion set; below 0.5 confidence, right only **29%**.

Title: Random Forests" (Leo Breiman, 2001)
Summary: - The **foundational random-forests paper** (Machine Learning 45(1):5–32). A random forest = a collection of tree classifiers `{h(x,Θk)}` where each tree is grown on an i.i.d. random vector Θ, and the trees **vote**. - Two theoretical results carry it: (1) by the **Strong Law of Large Numbers, forests converge** as you add trees — *more trees never overfit*; (2) generalization error is bounded by **strength** of individual trees and their **correlation**: `PE* ≤ ρ̄(1−s²)/s²`. - Accuracy **comparable to / better than AdaBoost**, more robust to noise, faster, and it ships **free internal estimates** (out-of-bag error, strength, correlation, variable importance). Local copy: [breiman-random-forests-2001.pdf](../assets/breiman-random-forests-2001.pdf); full text at `assets/breiman-random-forests-2001.txt`.

Title: Harvard MadSys — one year of LLM inference metadata traces, 6.12 billion requests, an open dataset hub for serving/systems research
Summary: Harvard's MadSys lab (Juncheng Yang, Assistant Professor, ex-CMU/Snowflake/AWS/Twitter/Cloudflare) announced a large open dataset of **LLM inference metadata**: one year of traces, **6.12 billion requests**, published at data.agentic-system.org, in collaboration with `@jon_durbin`, `@airesearch12`, and `@chutes_ai`. Intended to support research on real-world LLM serving workload characterization, systems design, and infrastructure optimization — a rare, large-scale empirical resource rather than a synthetic or small-scale benchmark.

Title: Jaana Dogan announces google/ax — \"we decided to reinvent Kubernetes for agentic workloads with statefulness and fast resumption,\" Google's open agentic orchestrator and runtime
Summary: The launch announcement for [[2026-09-20-google-ax-repo]] (Google's open agentic orchestrator) and its underlying runtime [[2026-05-13-agent-substrate-repo]], from Jaana Dogan — a well-known Google infrastructure engineer (formerly on the Go team, longtime observability/distributed-systems voice). The framing is explicit and load-bearing: "we decided to reinvent Kubernetes for agentic workloads with statefulness and fast resumption," plus a second, separate effort building "an agentic orchestrator that will be Google's open agentic orchestrator and runtime." High engagement (483.7K views, 3.3K likes) for an infrastructure-tooling announcement, reflecting how central agent-execution infrastructure has become as a topic.

Title: Free Mac notch apps, ranked (2026) — Notchy, Boring Notch, Atoll, NotchDrop, Sapphire
Summary: A five-item ranked listicle of free macOS "notch" apps — utilities that turn the MacBook camera notch into an iPhone-style Dynamic Island. One proprietary pick for "best free overall" (Notchy), then four open-source apps ordered by breadth and community size. Every item followed and verified below; the author's framing holds up, and the star counts confirm the ordering.

Title: DeepSpec — full-stack speculative-decoding training/eval codebase (DeepSeek-AI)
Summary: - **DeepSpec** is DeepSeek's MIT-licensed, "full-stack codebase for training and evaluating draft models for speculative decoding" — data prep → draft-model training → benchmark eval, all in one repo. - Ships **three draft-model algorithms**: **DSpark** (the new one → [[2026-06-27-dspark-speculative-decoding-paper]]), **DFlash**, and **Eagle3**. Targets Qwen3 and Gemma families. - Released alongside the DSpark paper + HF checkpoints (announced by [[2026-06-27-danielhanchen-dspark-announcement]]). **199★ → 993★ same day** (2026-06-27) — going viral fast.

Title: 20 subreddits to bookmark for a remote job hunt (Kenn_eth thread)
Summary: A 20-subreddit bookmark list for remote job hunting, plus a claim that engaging consistently trains Reddit's recommendation algorithm to surface better opportunities. The list itself is the whole substance — the surrounding advice is thin, and the replies push back hard on scams and pay.

Title: colibrì — run 744B–2.8T MoE models on consumer hardware by streaming experts from disk
Summary: A single-C-file inference engine that treats VRAM/RAM/NVMe as one memory tier and streams MoE experts from disk on demand, so a 744B-parameter model (GLM-5.2) runs on a 25 GB laptop. Eight model families share one `coli chat`/`serve`/`web` front end; the engine started on a 12-core laptop with 25 GB RAM and now has a community benchmark corpus behind it.

Title: Decision Trees and Ensemble Methods" — Stanford CS229 lecture (Raphael Townshend)
Summary: - The free Stanford **CS229: Machine Learning (Autumn 2018)** lecture on decision trees + ensembles, taught by **Raphael Townshend** (PhD candidate / Head TA; later founder of Atomic AI). ~100 min. Uploaded to the `stanfordonline` channel 2020-04-17. - This is the lecture the debunking post → [[2026-06-25-quant-hype-is-just-random-forests]] recommends: it builds **random forests from scratch at the board**, which is the "secret" behind the "77% pure-math quant" marketing. - Covers: decision trees (region-based, greedy CART splits, overfitting), then **bagging → random forests**, plus **boosting/AdaBoost** — analysed through the **bias–variance** lens.

Title: Agent Substrate Environment — a remote-driven, sandboxed dev-environment API on top of Substrate: shell commands, chunked file streaming, and a built-in MCP server (read/write/edit/glob/grep/shell)
Summary: Agent Substrate Environment (Apache-2.0, **26★**, alpha) is a thin, purpose-built "environment" API layered on [[2026-05-13-agent-substrate-repo]]: each environment is a Substrate actor (an isolated container) that clients drive remotely via a CLI, a Go/Python client library, or a built-in MCP server exposing `read_file`/`write_file`/`edit_file`/`glob`/`grep`/`shell`. Substrate provides the heavy lifting (snapshotting, scheduling, multiplexing many idle environments onto a small worker pool); this project adds the environment-shaped API most coding-agent harnesses actually want to call.

Title: Best Paper Awards in Computer Science (1996–2025)
Summary: A hand-curated index of **best/distinguished-paper awards across 32 major CS conferences, 1996–2025** — **1,819 papers** in total, maintained annually by Jeff Huang (Brown). The canonical "what did the field consider its best work each year" reference. Full extracted index (year · conference · title · authors) saved alongside as a grep-able asset.

Title: XHToken/Spark-X2.5 — Spark-X2.5 open model series
Summary: Official repo for Spark-X2.5-4B and -1.7B: compact general-purpose LLMs with a hybrid attention architecture (1 full-attention layer : 3 sliding-window layers) giving native 1M-token context, tuned for agentic/coding/reasoning workloads, Apache-2.0 licensed. 44 stars at capture.

Title: Mia-AiLab/Qwable-3.6-35b — Qwen3.6-35B fine-tuned on Fable-5-style traces
Summary: Full-capture of the model behind [[2026-06-22-qwable-35b-dgx-spark]]. A **full fine-tune of `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35b`** on a "cleaned Fable-5-style reasoning + instruction dataset" — name = **Qw**en + F**able**. MIT. For coding/debugging/local-agent use; GGUF-convertible.

Title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
Summary: **ICML 2024 Best Paper.** Tests scalable oversight via **debate**: two strong "expert" LLMs argue opposing answers and a weaker non-expert judge decides. Optimizing debaters for *persuasiveness* raises the judge's accuracy — weaker models can supervise stronger ones through debate. arXiv:2402.06782.

Title: SureForge — instruction-only Agent Skill for complex work (Da7-Tech)
Summary: - A **plain-text, no-runtime Agent Skill** that makes an agent *research before it asks, ask before it plans, plan before it builds, verify before it delivers, and get an independent review before calling anything done.* MIT, v1.0.0, **83★**, created **2026-09-09** (days old at capture). - It is the packaged, vendor-neutral version of the discipline I've assembled piecemeal: **ATTEST** (communication), **SUBSTANCE** (delivery), the `-nt` verify gates, and the vault's verification-gate notes — all in one installable skill. - Ships to **five hosts** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Hermes) via the `skills` CLI (`npx skills add Da7-Tech/SureForge`), and **ships its own eval + review harness** — the skill is treated as a product with a verifier.

Title: cordiverse/cordis — Meta-Framework of Spatiotemporal Composability
Summary: MIT, **8,163★**, 502 forks, created 2022-05-17, pushed 2026-09-06 (actively developed — same day as capture). Predates the paper by four years: Cordis is the working system the formalism was written *about*, not a reference implementation written to demonstrate it. The README carries an explicit stability warning: the API "is not yet stable and may change without notice."

Title: How to Build a Diffusion Language Model (Volodymyr Kuleshov)
Summary: An end-to-end tutorial on **diffusion language models (dLLMs)** — the model class that "went from open problem to reality in 2 years." Core idea: replace left-to-right autoregression with **masked/absorbing-state diffusion** (a BERT-like denoiser trained across all masking rates), giving parallel generation, error correction, and an inference-time compute↔quality knob. Kuleshov's thesis: *diffusion may be to inference-time scaling what the transformer was to pre-training scaling.*

Title: The Childhood Game That Reveals Why a Few Stocks Keep Crushing the Market — and the ETF Built Around It (advertorial for MPLY)
Summary: Uses the *Monopoly board game* as a hook for a genuine investing idea — **market concentration / economic moats** (companies with 50%+ market share, structural competitive advantages) — then pitches the **Monopoly ETF (ticker MPLY)** (Strategy Shares, PM Neil Azous, launched May 2025) as the way to buy it. Its headline "proof" is 20.4% vs 13.2% (S&P) over under 8 months — a promotional figure, not a track record.

Title: ARahim3/kaggle-tpu-lab — frontier-class open models on a free Kaggle TPU v5e-8 with an OpenAI/Anthropic endpoint
Summary: MIT-licensed recipes (Python/JAX) that turn a **free Kaggle TPU v5e-8** into a public endpoint speaking both the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, ~20 min from "Run" to URL. Two models today: **Qwen3.8-27B bf16** on vllm-tpu (+1 patch) at ~130 tok/s, and **GLM-5.3-Flash 320B MoE** on the author's own JAX/Pallas engine at ~64 tok/s, both at 262k context with prefix caching. Captured via [[2026-09-15-glm-5-3-flash-free-kaggle-tpu]].

Title: 2× DGX Spark running 64 concurrent Qwable-3.6-35b at ~150 tok/s
Summary: @losterror501 reports **2× DGX Spark running 64 concurrent instances of Qwable-3.6-35b at a combined ~150.0 tok/s**, crediting @MiaAI_lab's model.

Title: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems (LatentMAS)
Summary: LatentMAS lets LLM agents reason and communicate **entirely in continuous latent space** instead of text: each agent auto-regressively generates "latent thoughts" from its own last-layer hidden states (no decoding), and hands off to the next agent by concatenating layer-wise **KV caches** directly — no re-encoding, no lossy text summary. Training-free. Across 9 benchmarks and 5 model scales (Qwen3, Llama3), it beats single-model and text-based multi-agent-system (TextMAS) baselines while using **70.8–83.7% fewer output tokens** and running **4×–4.3× faster end-to-end**.

Title: Agent Substrate (Google, unofficial) — a secure-by-default execution runtime for millions of agent sandboxes, 10x container density, sub-500ms resume at 500+ activations/sec, framework-agnostic actor model on Kubernetes
Summary: Agent Substrate (Apache-2.0, **2,286★**) is a sandboxed execution runtime purpose-built for agent workloads specifically — not a general container platform. Its core move: map a large set of "actors" (stateful, mostly-idle agent applications) onto a small pool of "workers" (physical/VM capacity), exploiting the fact that agents spend most of their time idle to achieve heavy multiplexing. It claims **10x higher sandbox density than standard container runtimes**, **sub-500ms resume operations at over 500 suspend/resume activations per second**, and native zero-trust kernel/network isolation via gVisor and microVMs. Explicitly **not an SDK for building agents** — a system for running them at scale, framework-agnostic by design (ADK, LangChain, Claude Code, Codex, MCP servers all named as supported).

Title: Tencent Hunyuan's AuK audio model: launch-day ~25GB VRAM cut within a week via CPU offload, a ~7.5GB encoder trim, and an MLX branch for Apple Silicon
Summary: A one-week-later follow-up on Tencent Hunyuan's **AuK** ("nano banana for audio" — an open-source foundation model for unified speech generation and editing, launched 2026-09-10), reporting rapid post-launch VRAM optimization: from **~25 GB required on launch day** down to a smaller footprint via CPU offload, a **~7.5 GB cut to the encoder**, and an in-progress **MLX branch** for Apple Silicon support.

Title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
Summary: Trains agents to **manage their own working context as a first-class RL-learned skill**. Three moves over prior proactive-context-management work (StateLM, Sculptor, MemAct): (1) a richer 17-tool context toolset adding **planning, structured long-term memory, and soft offloading** (recoverable delete/compress/fold); (2) **context-aware partial rollout** — extra exploration budget branched at the context edits with the biggest context-length + entropy shifts; (3) **fine-grained credit assignment** — an intermediate snapshot's reward is the mean over all terminal trajectories passing through it, not the single trajectory's final reward (proven a lower-variance estimator of the same target). An 8B model with a 32K window then beats its own 128K-window backbone on long-context QA.

Title: Qwen3.8-27B abliterated at 240 tok/s with a 256K window on one RTX 5090 — @satellitedown releases fast-long-context
Summary: A three-post sequence from a hobbyist ("private datacenter owner") who could only reach ~160K context with an abliterated Qwen3.8-27B on a single RTX 5090 before VRAM ran out, then got the full 262,144-token window at 240–340 tok/s by quantising the KV cache to NVFP4 and patching SGLang. The captured post is the release pointer: a one-command launcher (`bash setup.sh`, menu 1/2/3) so newcomers can reproduce it, with an open invitation to "see if you can beat me". Full repo capture → [[2026-09-20-fast-long-context-repo]].

Title: Hyper-Extract — LLM knowledge-extraction CLI (text → graphs / hypergraphs / spatio-temporal)
Summary: A CLI + Python framework that turns arbitrary text (papers, earnings reports, contracts) into typed knowledge structures — and not just knowledge *graphs* but **hypergraphs** and **spatio-temporal graphs**, which the competitors (GraphRAG, LightRAG, KG-Gen, ATOM) don't do. 8 structures, 10+ extraction engines, 80+ zero-code YAML templates across 6 domains, incremental evolution, an **MCP server**, an **Agent-Skills bundle**, and — directly relevant to my vault — **export to an Obsidian vault of Markdown notes linked by `[[wikilinks]]`**. Works with Claude/GPT/Qwen/DeepSeek or fully local via vLLM.

Title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence (Technical Report)
Summary: Kimi K3 = 2.8T-total / 104B-active native-multimodal MoE with 1M context, built on KDA + Gated MLA hybrid attention, Attention Residuals, and Stable LatentMoE — claiming ~2.5× scaling efficiency over K2. Post-training centers on multi-effort agentic RL consolidated by multi-teacher on-policy distillation. Self-assessment: trails Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol overall; ahead of everything else evaluated, open or closed. Full weights released.

Title: SparkLLM open-sources Spark X2.5-4B & X2.5-1.7B — 1M-token native context on-device
Summary: SparkLLM open-sourced Spark-X2.5-4B and -1.7B, on-device models with a native 1M-token context via a hybrid full/sliding-window attention design, tuned for agents, code, math and instruction-following. Trained on ~20T tokens on domestic (Huawei Ascend) compute; runs on NVIDIA/Huawei/Hygon via vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, LM Studio.

Title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents (Pal, Wang, Buehler 2026)
Summary: Decentralized LLM agents coordinating **only through a shared world** (not conversation, roles, or a central workflow) build broader, more resilient technology **portfolios** than a strong best-of-N isolated-search baseline — but isolated search still wins the single **strongest** artifact. The swarm advantage is **bounded**: interaction buys collective coverage and a persistent technological ecology, not universally better individual inventions. ~95% of first technology adoption happens by **physical observation**, not by talking.

Title: Loop Engineering: The Anthropic Playbook for Designing Systems That Prompt Your Agents
Summary: A field study of **"Loop Engineering"** — named June 2026 (Osmani, independently Steinberger & Cherny) as the **fourth layer above prompt → context → harness engineering**. Unlike the others, it doesn't help you do the work better; it removes you from *doing the work at all* — you design the loop that prompts the agents and runs itself. The doc decomposes one loop turn into 5 moves / 6 parts, names the 5 failure modes and 4 silent costs, and closes with "stay the engineer." Local PDF: [loop-engineering-playbook.pdf](../assets/loop-engineering-playbook.pdf) · full text: [loop-engineering-playbook.txt](../assets/loop-engineering-playbook.txt).

Title: The Evaluation of the M365 Copilot Pilot in the Department for Business and Trade
Summary: 1,000 M365 Copilot licences, 3-month pilot (Oct–Dec 2024), evaluated by DBT's own analysts. High satisfaction (72%), small self-reported time savings on written tasks, some tasks made *slower*, and **no robust evidence that time savings translated into productivity**. The observed-task sessions are the sharp part: on three of four tasks Copilot users were faster, worse, or both.

Title: Jev's Architecture Unmasked (Archer Hume) — reverse-engineering TypeSafe's closed decision model from 10,000+ API calls: shared-state KV cache, isolated question branches, listwise options, direct probability readouts
Summary: Archer Hume probes TypeSafe's closed Jev API (latency, token accounting, adversarial prompt placement, option-set perturbation) and reconstructs it as a causal transformer with **seven properties**: direct probability readouts (linear head + softmax, no generation), one shared-state encoding that all questions read, isolated per-question branches that cannot see each other, **listwise** option interaction (adding an irrelevant option measurably shifts the log-odds between existing ones), outcome-trained distributions via RLCD with a proper scoring rule, probably a sparse MoE backbone (~10B active — "least certain"), and batch-scheduled branches over a shared KV cache. Measured: 1,500 questions in a median 610 ms; a 30k-token state in 218 ms; MMLU-Pro 84.6%; ECE 0.0313 on MMLU. Announces an open-weight rebuild "trained on the inferred design" — not released. Tweet 1,512 likes / 198k views.

Title: dnhkng/RYS — layer-duplication ('relayering') reproducibility repo
Summary: The full reproducibility codebase behind [[2026-03-10-rys-llm-neuroanatomy]] and [[2026-03-22-rys-ii-llm-neuroanatomy]]: config notation, probe datasets (math/EQ-Bench), the (i,j) sweep, beam search, XGBoost surrogate, and HuggingFace export tooling for the RYS layer-duplicated models. 80 stars, no license file (unclear-license — check before reuse).

Title: AI Research Preference Models
Summary: FAIR at Meta introduces AI Research Preference Models (RPMs): a component bolted onto an AI research agent (AIRA) that ranks unexecuted candidate ML experiments — instead of running all of them — so scarce GPU budget goes to the most promising one. Two variants (inference-only reasoning, and agentic with pilot experiments) lift AIRA-dojo's average normalized score on AIRS-Bench from 0.684 to 0.711 and 0.729 respectively, and reach baseline-final performance in ~15 of 24 hours using under two-thirds the compute.

Title: Feyospace-v1 — how the "Cyber Mercury Seven" trained frontier cyber models
Summary: - A seven-person independent team ("Cyber Mercury Seven") post-trained **three small open-weight Qwen checkpoints** into cybersecurity models (**Feyospace-v1**) that rank **#1 at their parameter-size classes** on cyber benchmarks. - The method is **data-centric SFT** — no RL claimed — on **164,269 execution-verified trajectories** distilled from frontier teacher models into resettable CVE / CTF / kernel / exploit / firmware environments. - The lead model **Feyospace-s1**: **63.24% verified success rate**, **10th on the official CyberGym leaderboard** (1st at its size). Aggregate: **+23.76%** on CyberGym, **+10.49%** on pooled CTF suites. - The "how" is the story: the data engine leans on **ToS-violating teacher extraction** — gray-market accounts (~273× cost efficiency), jailbreak/mutation to bypass teacher API restrictions, and recovery of hidden reasoning traces. Legally/ethically fraught, and it makes the results hard to reproduce cleanly.
